subject: Chemistry
central_question: How do the structures of carbonyl and carboxyl groups determine the preparation, physical properties, acidity and reactions of aldehydes, ketones and carboxylic acids?
in_scope_units: Nomenclature and planar, polar structure of aldehyde and ketone carbonyl groups.
General and selective methods for preparing aldehydes and ketones.
Physical properties of aldehydes and ketones.
Nucleophilic addition and important chemical reactions of aldehydes and ketones.
Oxidation, reduction, alpha-hydrogen reactions, aldol condensation and Cannizzaro reaction.
Chemical tests distinguishing aldehydes and ketones.
Nomenclature and structure of carboxylic acids.
Preparation, physical properties, acidity and substituent effects in carboxylic acids.
Reactions and uses of carboxylic acids.
banned_topics: Alcohol chemistry except where used as a precursor or product, which belongs to the previous chapter.
Detailed mechanisms of every named reaction beyond those selected in the chapter.
Amides and acyl halides as full independent functional-group chapters; they appear here mainly as derivatives or reagents.

known_pitfalls.claim: Ketones are more reactive than aldehydes toward nucleophilic addition.
known_pitfalls.correction: Aldehydes are generally more reactive because they have less steric hindrance and less electron donation from alkyl groups.
Aliphatic aldehydes generally reduce Fehling’s solution, whereas aromatic aldehydes such as benzaldehyde usually do not.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every carbonyl compound undergoes aldol condensation.
known_pitfalls.correction: Aldehydes or ketones need at least one alpha hydrogen to form the enolate required for aldol reaction.

known_pitfalls.claim: Carboxylic acids are acidic because the neutral acid has many resonance structures.
known_pitfalls.correction: Their acidity is mainly due to resonance stabilisation of the carboxylate conjugate base.
Electron-withdrawing groups stabilise the carboxylate ion and increase acidity; electron-donating groups generally decrease it.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with NCERT Example 8.1 on reagent selection for aldehyde and ketone preparations.
Use NCERT Example 8.2 for boiling-point order and intermolecular forces.
Apply NCERT Example 8.3 to compare benzaldehyde and propanal reactivity.
Use NCERT Example 8.4 for structure identification from derivative and oxidation data.
Finish with NCERT Example 8.5 for carboxylic-acid transformations.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end-of-chapter Exercises are numbered 8.1 to 8.20 and cover nomenclature, preparations, nucleophilic additions, tests, aldol and Cannizzaro reactions, acidity, carboxylic-acid reactions and conversions.
